Container.Name: Hearth
Container.Overview: Hearth is a chat app for friend groups and small communities that you host yourself: servers with text and voice channels, roles, threads, direct messages and group chats, voice and video calls with screen sharing, and watching videos together. Messages, files and calls are end-to-end encrypted in the app, so the server stores only encrypted data (it still sees who talks to whom, and when). One process and a SQLite file; free and MIT licensed.[br][br] [b]First run:[/b] open the WebUI and click through the certificate warning once (Hearth makes its own certificate; browsers only allow encryption and microphones on https). The first account to sign up becomes the owner, so sign up before you share the address.[br][br] [b]Friends outside your network[/b] need a domain or a tunnel (Cloudflare Tunnel, Tailscale Funnel, or a reverse proxy with a real certificate). Behind a proxy that does https, set HTTPS to false and TRUST_PROXY to the proxy's address. Big group video calls don't scale: calls go directly between people (best with up to about 4 to 6 cameras).

Config.Name: WebUI (https)
Config.Description: Hearth's web app, desktop and Android apps, and invite links all use this port. It speaks https with its own certificate unless HTTPS is false.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: The database, uploads, the server's keys and certificate, and backups. Back this folder up.

Config.Name: PUBLIC_HOSTS
Config.Description: Extra names or addresses for Hearth's own certificate, comma-separated: this server's LAN address, a public IP or a dynamic DNS name (e.g. 192.168.1.20,myhearth.duckdns.org). After changing it, delete cert.pem and key.pem from the Data folder and restart.

Config.Name: HTTPS
Config.Description: true: Hearth serves https itself (self-signed certificate). false: only behind a reverse proxy or tunnel that does https; plain http from the internet is refused.

Config.Name: TRUST_PROXY
Config.Description: Only with a reverse proxy or tunnel: its address or subnet, so each visitor keeps their own address for bans and sign-in limits. Leave empty without one. Never a number or Docker's gateway while the port is reachable from other machines.

Config.Name: REGISTRATION_CODE
Config.Description: Optional: a code people need to sign up. Registration can also be closed in Admin, Registration and Terms.

Config.Name: INSTANCE_NAME
Config.Description: Name shown in the browser tab and on the sign-in screen.
